explanation_en: A common collocation used to describe a place of intense activity, conflict, or danger (a 'hotspot'). It is frequently used in news reports regarding geopolitics, crime, or social unrest. It can also refer to a Wi-Fi hotspot, but in this context, it has a political/security meaning.

examples.en_text: The police have increased surveillance in the city's hotspots to reduce crime.
examples.target_text: La policía ha aumentado la vigilancia en los puntos calientes de la ciudad para reducir la delincuencia.

examples.en_text: This map shows the trouble spots on the highway where most traffic accidents occur.
examples.target_text: Este mapa muestra los puntos calientes de la carretera donde ocurren más accidentes de tráfico.

examples.en_text: Tropical rainforests are considered biodiversity hotspots that we must protect.
examples.target_text: Las selvas tropicales son consideradas puntos calientes de biodiversidad que debemos proteger.

examples.en_text: The UN special envoy will visit the conflict's trouble spots to seek a peaceful solution.
examples.target_text: El enviado especial de la ONU visitará los puntos calientes del conflicto para buscar una solución pacífica.

examples.en_text: Health authorities are monitoring the hotspots where more cases of the virus have been detected.
examples.target_text: Las autoridades sanitarias están vigilando los puntos calientes donde se han detectado más casos del virus.

examples.en_text: The marketing department identified the hotspots in the store where customers spend the most time.
examples.target_text: El departamento de marketing identificó los puntos calientes de la tienda donde los clientes pasan más tiempo.

explanation_en: A metaphorical expression meaning to draw attention to, focus on, or highlight a specific issue. It comes from the theater/lighting terminology ('foco' meaning spotlight). It is widely used in journalism, politics, and business discussions.

examples.en_text: The new marketing plan focuses on social media to attract young people.
examples.target_text: El nuevo plan de marketing pone el foco en las redes sociales para atraer a los jóvenes.

examples.en_text: In this course, we focus on practice and not so much on theory.
examples.target_text: En este curso, ponemos el foco en la práctica y no tanto en la teoría.

examples.en_text: Yesterday's documentary shone a spotlight on the problems of marine pollution.
examples.target_text: El documental de ayer puso el foco en los problemas de la contaminación marina.

examples.en_text: Many doctors focus on the importance of sleeping well to reduce stress.
examples.target_text: Muchos médicos ponen el foco en la importancia de dormir bien para reducir el estrés.

examples.en_text: It is important that we focus on the quality of customer service this week.
examples.target_text: Es importante que pongamos el foco en la calidad del servicio al cliente esta semana.

examples.en_text: If you want to improve your health, you must focus on your daily diet.
examples.target_text: Si quieres mejorar tu salud, debes poner el foco en tu alimentación diaria.

explanation_en: This idiom means to support, defend, or take the side of a person, group, or institution in a conflict or debate. It is the opposite of 'ponerse en contra de' (to oppose) or 'ponerse de perfil' (to remain neutral/avoid taking a stand). It is highly useful for discussing debates and political alignments.

examples.en_text: In that argument, María decided to side with the director.
examples.target_text: En esa discusión, María decidió ponerse del lado del director.

examples.en_text: The government should side with the workers in this crisis.
examples.target_text: El gobierno debería ponerse del lado de los trabajadores en esta crisis.

examples.en_text: I don't understand why you sided with the client when he wasn't right.
examples.target_text: No entiendo por qué te pusiste del lado del cliente si él no tenía razón.

examples.en_text: In the end, the judge sided with the accused.
examples.target_text: Al final, el juez se puso del lado del acusado.

examples.en_text: The teacher always sides with the weakest student.
examples.target_text: La profesora siempre se pone del lado del alumno más débil.

examples.en_text: In yesterday's debate, most of the deputies sided with the people.
examples.target_text: En el debate de ayer, la mayoría de los diputados se pusieron del lado del pueblo.

explanation_en: A dramatic and highly idiomatic expression meaning to leave someone without help, resources, or protection, letting whatever happens to them be determined by chance or fate. It is often used in passive constructions ('ser abandonado a su suerte') or with the verb 'dejar' ('dejar a alguien a su suerte').

examples.en_text: After the storm, many pets were left to their fate in the streets.
examples.target_text: Tras la tormenta, muchos animales domésticos quedaron abandonados a su suerte en las calles.

examples.en_text: The tour guide left and left the young traveler to his fate in the middle of the mountain.
examples.target_text: El guía turístico se fue y dejó al joven viajero abandonado a su suerte en medio de la montaña.

examples.en_text: The families in that mountainous region feel they have been left to their fate by the government.
examples.target_text: Las familias de esa región montañosa sienten que han sido abandonadas a su suerte por el gobierno.

examples.en_text: Without the support of her partners, the director felt left to her own devices to resolve the company's crisis.
examples.target_text: Sin el apoyo de sus socios, la directora se sintió abandonada a su suerte para resolver la crisis de la empresa.

examples.en_text: Due to the pilots' strike, hundreds of passengers were left to fend for themselves at the airport.
examples.target_text: Debido a la huelga de pilotos, cientos de pasajeros quedaron abandonados a su suerte en el aeropuerto.

examples.en_text: If we don't take care of this national park, the forest will be left to its fate and will end up disappearing.
examples.target_text: Si no cuidamos este parque nacional, el bosque quedará abandonado a su suerte y terminará desapareciendo.

explanation_en: Used before a noun to indicate that something is happening at the very peak, middle, or height of an event or period (e.g., 'en pleno verano', 'en plena crisis'). It agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies. It adds emphasis and a sense of intensity to the context.

examples.en_text: His phone died in the middle of a work meeting.
examples.target_text: Se le apagó el teléfono en plena reunión de trabajo.

examples.en_text: We ran out of gas in the middle of the highway.
examples.target_text: Nos quedamos sin gasolina en plena autopista.

examples.en_text: The actor forgot his lines in the middle of the performance.
examples.target_text: El actor olvidó su texto en plena actuación.

examples.en_text: I woke up in the middle of the night because of a strange noise.
examples.target_text: Me desperté en plena noche por culpa de un ruido extraño.

examples.en_text: They decided to travel to Paris at the height of the high season.
examples.target_text: Decidieron viajar a París en plena temporada alta.

examples.en_text: It started to rain heavily when we were right in the middle of the street.
examples.target_text: Empezó a llover con fuerza cuando estábamos en plena calle.

explanation_en: This common expression means 'to cope', 'to handle', or 'to keep up with demand'. It is almost always used in the negative ('no dar abasto') to indicate that resources, staff, or capacity are overwhelmed by demand. It is highly frequent in both colloquial speech and news reports.

examples.en_text: With so many new emails every day, the secretary can't keep up.
examples.target_text: Con tantos correos nuevos cada día, el secretario no da abasto.

examples.en_text: There are too many customers on the terrace and the waiters can't cope with the demand.
examples.target_text: Hay demasiados clientes en la terraza y los camareros no dan abasto.

examples.en_text: During the sale season, the store couldn't keep up with the orders.
examples.target_text: Durante la temporada de rebajas, la tienda no daba abasto con los pedidos.

examples.en_text: I have three exams this week and I can't keep up with the studying.
examples.target_text: Tengo tres exámenes esta semana y no doy abasto con el estudio.

examples.en_text: The delivery company needs to hire more people because it can't cope with the demand.
examples.target_text: La empresa de mensajería necesita contratar a más gente porque no puede dar abasto.

examples.en_text: With four young children at home, my husband and I can't keep up.
examples.target_text: Con cuatro niños pequeños en casa, mi esposo y yo no damos abasto.

explanation_en: 'A tope' is a very common colloquial expression meaning 'full to capacity', 'packed', or 'at full throttle/maximum'. It can describe a place crowded with people, a schedule that is extremely busy, or working at maximum effort. It is highly natural and widely used in Spain.

examples.en_text: The downtown bar was packed on Saturday night, so we went somewhere else.
examples.target_text: El bar del centro estaba a tope el sábado por la noche, así que fuimos a otro lugar.

examples.en_text: Whenever I take the subway at eight in the morning, the cars are packed to capacity.
examples.target_text: Siempre que tomo el metro a las ocho de la mañana, los vagones van a tope.

examples.en_text: The theater was full to capacity for the last performance of the season.
examples.target_text: El teatro estaba a tope para la última función de la temporada.

examples.en_text: In August, all the coastal hotels are fully booked and it's almost impossible to reserve.
examples.target_text: En agosto, todos los hoteles de la costa están a tope y es casi imposible reservar.

examples.en_text: I don't like going to that pool in the summer because it is always packed with kids.
examples.target_text: No me gusta ir a esa piscina en verano porque siempre está a tope de niños.

examples.en_text: We had to park very far away because the shopping mall parking lot was completely full.
examples.target_text: Tuvimos que aparcar muy lejos porque el aparcamiento del centro comercial estaba a tope.

explanation_en: The construction 'nada más' followed by an infinitive is a common way to say 'as soon as' or 'immediately upon doing something'. It is a very natural grammatical pattern in Spanish that replaces 'tan pronto como' or 'en cuanto'. It is widely used in spoken Spanish across all registers.

examples.en_text: As soon as you turn around, you will see the cathedral on your right.
examples.target_text: Nada más girarte, verás la catedral a tu derecha.

examples.en_text: As soon as I turned around, I realized I had lost my keys.
examples.target_text: Nada más girarme, me di cuenta de que había perdido las llaves.

examples.en_text: As soon as she turned around, she saw her former boss in the coffee shop.
examples.target_text: Nada más girarse, ella vio a su antiguo jefe en la cafetería.

examples.en_text: As soon as we turned around, the bus closed its doors and left.
examples.target_text: Nada más girarnos, el autobús cerró las puertas y se fue.

examples.en_text: As soon as they turned around for the photo, it started to rain heavily.
examples.target_text: Nada más girarse para la foto, empezó a llover con fuerza.

examples.en_text: Be careful; as soon as you turn around you are going to bump into that table.
examples.target_text: Ten cuidado; nada más girarte vas a chocar con esa mesa.

explanation_en: 'Presagio' means omen or sign of a future event. The collocation 'los peores presagios' (the worst omens/fears) is commonly used in news and literature to describe a situation where things are expected to turn out very badly. It often collocates with verbs like 'traer', 'confirmar', or 'cumplirse'.

examples.en_text: In the end, the storm destroyed the harvest and the worst fears were realized.
examples.target_text: Al final, la tormenta destruyó la cosecha y se cumplieron los peores presagios.

examples.en_text: The economists' worst fears were confirmed with the drop in sales.
examples.target_text: Los peores presagios de los economistas se confirmaron con la caída de las ventas.

examples.en_text: The doctor gave us good news, refuting the family's worst fears.
examples.target_text: El médico nos dio una buena noticia, desmintiendo los peores presagios de la familia.

examples.en_text: The captain's injury confirmed the worst fears for tomorrow's match.
examples.target_text: La lesión del capitán confirmó los peores presagios para el partido de mañana.

examples.en_text: Despite the worst fears, the project was a great success and we finished on time.
examples.target_text: A pesar de los peores presagios, el proyecto fue un gran éxito y terminamos a tiempo.

examples.en_text: When they found the empty car, the worst fears began to gain strength.
examples.target_text: Cuando encontraron el coche vacío, los peores presagios empezaron a tomar fuerza.

explanation_en: 'Un revés' means a setback, reverse, or blow. It is a very common B2/C1 noun used in journalism and formal speech to describe an unexpected obstacle or negative turn of events. It frequently collocates with verbs like 'suponer', 'sufrir', or 'dar'.

examples.en_text: The cancellation of the contract was an additional setback for the company.
examples.target_text: La cancelación del contrato fue un revés adicional para la empresa.

examples.en_text: Missing the afternoon train was an additional setback for our trip.
examples.target_text: Perder el tren de la tarde supuso un revés adicional para nuestro viaje.

examples.en_text: The star forward's injury is an additional setback for the team before the final match.
examples.target_text: La lesión del delantero estrella es un revés adicional para el equipo antes del partido final.

examples.en_text: Just when we thought everything was going well, this traffic ticket was an additional setback.
examples.target_text: Justo cuando pensábamos que todo iba bien, esta multa de tráfico fue un revés adicional.

examples.en_text: Last night's storm caused an additional setback for the roadworks.
examples.target_text: La tormenta de anoche causó un revés adicional para las obras de la carretera.

examples.en_text: Catching the flu during his recovery was an additional setback for the patient.
examples.target_text: Contraer una gripe durante su recuperación fue un revés adicional para el paciente.

explanation_en: 'Dar lugar a' is a very common Spanish idiom meaning 'to give rise to', 'to lead to', or 'to cause'. It is used in both formal and informal contexts to express causality. It is a key connective phrase for B2/C1 learners to structure arguments and explanations naturally.

examples.en_text: The lack of communication in a couple often gives rise to misunderstandings.
examples.target_text: La falta de comunicación en la pareja a menudo da lugar a malentendidos.

examples.en_text: These new economic measures give rise to many protests in the street.
examples.target_text: Estas nuevas medidas económicas dan lugar a muchas protestas en la calle.

examples.en_text: Yesterday's strong wind gave rise to several accidents on the highway.
examples.target_text: El fuerte viento de ayer dio lugar a varios accidentes en la carretera.

examples.en_text: A small mistake in the contract can give rise to serious legal problems.
examples.target_text: Un pequeño error en el contrato puede dar lugar a serios problemas legales.

examples.en_text: Too much rain at this time of year gives rise to the appearance of fungi on the plants.
examples.target_text: El exceso de lluvia en esta época da lugar a la aparición de hongos en las plantas.

examples.en_text: Social networks sometimes give rise to very intense debates among users.
examples.target_text: Las redes sociales a veces dan lugar a debates muy intensos entre los usuarios.

explanation_en: 'De lo contrario' is a fixed phrase meaning 'otherwise' or 'if not'. It is used to introduce the negative consequence of not fulfilling the previously mentioned condition. It is a highly useful transition word in both spoken and written Spanish, typical of B2/C1 proficiency.

examples.en_text: You have to leave for the airport now; otherwise, you're going to miss the flight.
examples.target_text: Tienes que salir ya para el aeropuerto; de lo contrario, vas a perder el vuelo.

examples.en_text: It is important to drink enough water, otherwise you could get a headache.
examples.target_text: Es importante beber suficiente agua, de lo contrario podrías tener dolor de cabeza.

examples.en_text: We must submit the report today; otherwise, the boss is going to get angry.
examples.target_text: Debemos entregar el informe hoy; de lo contrario, el jefe se va a enfadar.

examples.en_text: Take an umbrella with you, otherwise you are going to get wet if it starts to rain.
examples.target_text: Lleva un paraguas contigo, de lo contrario te vas a mojar si empieza a llover.

examples.en_text: Save the document right now; otherwise, you will lose all the changes.
examples.target_text: Guarda el documento ahora mismo; de lo contrario, perderás todos los cambios.

examples.en_text: Please confirm your attendance before Friday; otherwise, we won't be able to reserve your spot.
examples.target_text: Por favor, confirma tu asistencia antes del viernes; de lo contrario, no podremos reservar tu sitio.
